http://www.euronews.com/2026/07/30/frenc.text: Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, 19, was handed a SG$600 (€406) fine after admitting to posting to social media a video of himself putting a straw he had licked back into the dispenser of an orange juice vending machine.Maximilien, who is studying in Singapore, posted a video of himself executing the prank on Instagram with the caption "city is not safe".The clip went viral on Instagram shortly after the incident on March 12, triggering a backlash that led to his arrest in Singapore, which is known for its strict enforcement of public order and hygiene rules.Handing down the sentence, Judge Kelly Ho said given Maximilien's "age and nature of the offence", alternatives such as probation or a community-based sentence would not be imposed.Prosecutors agreed to the defence's proposal for a fine, saying the offence was at the "lower end" of its seriousness and while hygiene was compromised, no member of the public used the straw, so there "was no evidence of harm".They added that Maximilien "pleaded guilty at the earliest possible opportunity."In Singapore, public nuisance offenders face up to SG$2000 (€1353) fine and three months in jail."He is fully sorry for having caused all this trouble," Maximilien's defence counsel Kalidass Murugaiyan told the judge.iJooz vending machines are a common sight in shopping districts, selling freshly-squeezed orange juice for SG$2 (€1.35) a cup. The company said it replaced all 500 straws in the machine dispenser after the teenager's prank.Singapore is known for its no-nonsense approach to public stunts.Last year it deported an Australian man at the end of a nine-day jail term for rushing film star Ariana Grande during the Asian premiere of "Wicked: For Good".

https://brooklyneagle.com/404797/estonia.text: Estonian pleads guilty to selling electronics to Russia DOWNTOWN BROOKLYN – AN ESTONIAN MAN admitted in Brooklyn federal court on Thursday to his role in a scheme to illegally export over $1 million in sensitive electronic components to Russia, according to Joseph Nocella Jr., U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York. Andrey Shevlyakov pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit export violations, faces up to 40 years’ imprisonment, and will forfeit $1.5 million to the government. Shevlyakov had been added to a list of persons prohibited from acquiring items from the U.S. without the Department of Commerce’s permission. Using shell companies, Shevlyakov deceived suppliers and bought sensitive technology anyway. He then shipped the goods – including components used in communications, avionics, missiles and electronic warfare systems – to Russian defense contractors and government agencies. In one instance, Shevlyakov placed an order with a U.S. company for sensitive electronic components, but the company refused to sell to him. Shevlyakov then canceled his order, only to place it again days later under a false name. Shevlyakov was also involved in making deliveries, crossing from Estonia into Russia over 100 times between 2010 and 2016, according to border records. Additionally, Finnish border authorities once caught him with €70,000 worth of electronics hidden in his vehicle, the U.S. attorney’s office said. ✰✰✰ Subscribe to Continue Reading Sign In Explore https://allhiphop.com/news/ye-performs-p.text: Skip to main content Skip to header right navigation Skip to site footer Ye Performs Portugal Concert Despite International Pressure Ye performs a clean set for 34,000 fans at Portugal’s Algarve Stadium, defying international pressure and diplomatic calls for the concert’s cancellation. Mike Winslow • Aug 9, 2026 @ 1:02 PM Kanye West - InstarImages Ye pulled off what seemed impossible in Portugal on Friday night, performing in front of 34,000 fans at Estádio do Algarve despite mounting international pressure to cancel the show. The concert marked a rare victory for the rapper’s controversial “Bully” tour, which has faced cancellations across Europe and visa denials in multiple countries. According to Euronews , the Algarve performance went smoothly, with Ye delivering tracks like “Stronger,” “Gold Digger,” and “American Boy” while standing atop the famous giant globe on the stadium pitch. The concert also featured a special moment when Ye invited his daughter, North West, on stage for a duet, giving fans a rare glimpse of a family collaboration. Join Us AllHipHop’s Daily News Service Delivering news to inboxes since 1999. We break it. They take it. Get it first, straight from AllHipHop. Sign up for exclusives The Israeli ambassador to Portugal, Oren Rozenblat, had publicly called for the concert’s cancellation just days before, citing Ye’s history of antisemitic statements and declarations of support for Nazism. Rozenblat’s video message condemned what he characterized as hate speech rather than provocation, pointing to the rapper’s past comments glorifying Hitler and claiming slavery was a choice. Yet Portugal’s government and event organizers stood firm, with the concert’s promoter dismissing the controversy as “misinformation” and arguing there was no legitimate security threat to public order. Ye’s international tour has become a masterclass in controversy management, with shows canceled in the UK, France, Poland, Italy, and the Czech Republic. The rapper attempted damage control by publishing a full-page apology in the Wall Street Journal, describing his past behavior as stemming from “a four-month manic episode of psychotic, paranoid and impulsive behavior” and claiming he “lost touch with reality.” The performance came as part of the ongoing promotion of his 12th studio album, Bully , which has been overshadowed by the legal and reputational challenges surrounding the artist. The rapper’s next scheduled appearance is in Kazakhstan at the Central Stadium in Almaty on August 14, followed by performances in New Orleans on August 28 and Chicago on September 3, 2026. Photograph: Steven Saphore/AAP New South Wales Woman’s body found in stockyard trough close to NSW-Queensland border Police say body found by trail bike riders at remote farm in Terragon is badly decomposed, sparking search of missing persons records Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Tue 6 Oct 2026 05.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A partially submerged body believed to be a woman has been discovered in a remote stockyard, with the death being treated as suspicious. Officers were called to a property in Terragon, near Murwillumbah in northern NSW , at about 11.20am on Monday after reports of a dead body. The body, which is yet to be identified, was found partially submerged in a disused stock dip, a large trough commonly used to bathe livestock in anti-parasite solutions, police said. Police said the body was badly decomposed. “The body is believed to be of a female, but due to the state of decomposition of that body I’m unable to provide further details,” Det Insp Matthew Zimmer told reporters in Tweed Heads on Tuesday. “Due to the location of the body, the remoteness of the area, the absence of a vehicle or any other mode of transport, we are treating this death as suspicious.” He said it was difficult to determine how long the remains had been at the site. The grim discovery was made by two trail bike riders in an area deemed crown land. A crime scene was set up overnight, with specialist forensic examiners combing the area. Police were checking through missing persons registers in NSW and Queensland, Zimmer said. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion A postmortem examination is expected to be carried out in coming days to help identify the body and the cause of death. Terragon is located in Tweed Shire, roughly 40km from the NSW-Queensland border.
